subject: Clarifying VPC/on-prem privacy boundaries and customer-controlled keys
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@rodin-analytics.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@rodin-analytics.com
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying privacy boundaries for VPC/on-prem deployment with customer KMS

Diego —

Thanks for the intro last week. We're evaluating Redwood's private deployment option (VPC + on‑prem connector) and need to confirm a few points before we can proceed to legal review. High-level questions below — I've attached our questionnaire for reference (rodin-privacy-questionnaire.pdf).

1) Keys: we plan to use our KMS (BYOK). Can you confirm whether Redwood ever holds or can reconstruct customer private keys? What does your key rotation / escrow policy look like?

2) Operator access: under what circumstances would Redwood engineers have access to customer data or models? Do you enforce break‑glass approval flows and documented timeboxed sessions?

3) Telemetry & logs: what telemetry is collected from private deployments? Is raw request/response content ever captured or stored by Redwood? Where are logs retained and can they be routed to our S3?

4) Subprocessors & transfers: please share an up‑to‑date subprocessors list and confirm whether any subprocessors process cross‑border. We need to know if any transfers to non‑EEA regions can occur without prior consent.

5) DPA: we'd like to see a draft DPA that reflects BYOK and limited operator access.

Can we schedule a 30‑minute call this week to walk through? Prefer Sept 8th morning PT.

Appreciate it —
Samantha
Head of Security Operations
Rodin Analytics

[Attachment: rodin-privacy-questionnaire.pdf]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@rodin-analytics.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying privacy boundaries for VPC/on-prem deployment with customer KMS

Samantha —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear questions. Quick responses inline, and I attached a starter DPA draft and a keystore responsibility CSV so your legal/ops can iterate (redwood-dpa-draft-v1.pdf, keystore_responsibility_matrix.csv).

1) Keys: Redwood supports customer‑managed keys (BYOK). We do not persist customer private keys in our control plane. Our recommended pattern is envelope encryption where your KMS holds root keys; Redwood stores only encrypted data keys. We do not perform key escrow unless explicitly requested and contractually defined (we can add an escrow addendum if needed).

2) Operator access: Operator access is limited to timeboxed support sessions with explicit customer approval. Access requires a ticket reference and is logged; we provide audit records on request. For private deployments we can enforce a no‑operator‑data‑view policy for sensitive request bodies — telemetry will be minimized (see below).

3) Telemetry & logs: By default we collect metrics (latency, per‑route error rates) and service telemetry. Request/response payloads are NOT retained by Redwood for private deployments unless you enable a support capture (and then only for the window you approve). We can configure log forwarding to your S3 or an on‑prem ELK — we surface a per‑route toggle for PII redaction.

4) Subprocessors & transfers: We'll attach our subprocessors list in the formal DPA; the short answer: cloud infra, monitoring vendor, and CDNs are the likely subprocessors. For private deployments we can use region‑bound capacity and restrict data flows to the region you designate; transfers outside the region require your approval.

5) DPA: attached draft includes BYOK clauses and operator access controls. Please flag any edits and we'll incorporate.

Next steps:
- Please confirm availability for a technical + legal call on Sept 8 at 09:30 PT (we can host remote demo of the keystore handshake).
- If Rodin needs an air‑gapped/on‑prem-only option, note that in replies and we'll route to the Private Deploy engineering team.

I'll let Irene and Karthik add more detail on legal/ops and networking.

Best,
Diego
Head of Product — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-dpa-draft-v1.pdf, keystore_responsibility_matrix.csv]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@rodin-analytics.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-08T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying privacy boundaries for VPC/on-prem deployment with customer KMS

Samantha —

I've reviewed Diego's responses and attached a marked‑up DPA that tracks the BYOK and operator constraints we discussed (dpa-markup.docx). A few legal clarifications up front:

• Key custody: Redwood's standard position is no retention of customer private keys. If Rodin requires an escrow or notarized key recovery process, that should be spelled out in an addendum (we can provide language).

• Access windows: Operator access is strictly emergency or investigative and requires: (a) customer written approval per ticket, (b) timeboxed session with MFA, and (c) full session recording and audit log export. We can include a clause giving Rodin the option to reject operator sessions entirely for production environments.

• Logs & evidence: We can ship full audit logs to a customer S3 bucket on a retention schedule you choose. For compliance reviews we can also provide SOC 2 attestation materials under NDA.

• Subprocessors & transfers: We'll commit to a subprocessors notification period (30 days) and require Rodin signoff if you want any data processed outside the designated US region.

I'll incorporate any precise language requests from your counsel. Happy to be on the call — I propose Sept 8 at 09:30 PT.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dpa-markup.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@rodin-analytics.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying privacy boundaries for VPC/on-prem deployment with customer KMS

Hi Samantha —

Technical follow‑up from infra side after our review:

- Network zoning: for a VPC/private deployment we can compartmentalize control plane telemetry and customer data plane into separate subnets. See attached network_zones.png.

- KMS handshake: we support HSM‑backed customer KMS (BYOK). The recommended flow is an envelope pattern — Redwood never retains your unwrapped data keys. If you require an on‑prem HSM connector we can run an agent in your DMZ to avoid key egress.

- Telemetry minimization: we can enable a minimal telemetry profile that only emits metrics and anonymized resource traces (no request bodies). If you want additional guarantees we can sign a clause to prohibit collection of any content payloads except under explicit, ticketed support captures.

Proposed mutual action items and timeline:
1) Legal: Rodin reviews redwood‑dpa‑draft‑v1 + dpa‑markup and returns comments (target: Sept 14).
2) Technical: agree keystore handshake and test plan; dry run of key rotation (target: Sept 21).
3) Ops: confirm log forwarding + retention policy and subprocessors acceptance (target: Sept 18).

I've attached the network diagram and the keystore responsibility matrix for your engineers to compare with your existing controls. If this timeline works I'll create a short project plan in HubSpot and a DocuSign envelope for the DPA.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect — Private Deploys
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: network_zones.png, keystore_responsibility_matrix.csv]
